newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's population hits estimated 93 million.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's population hits estimated 93 million.

text.p: Mexico's population has shot up by more than 11 million in the last seven years to an estimated 93 million now, but the rate of growth is falling, the national statistics institute INEGI said Monday.
The sharp increase has made Mexico the 11th most populous nation and more than doubled its size in the last 25 years, INEGI said, reporting the final results of its 1995 census.
But the agency said Mexico's population was currently growing by just under 1.8 percent a year, down from 2.3 percent a year during the 1980s.
The birthrate was still way above the level of most industrialised nations but should fall further in coming years if present trends continued, it said.

The figures showed an increasingly urbanized country. A quarter of the population live in the three biggest cities -- Mexico City, Guadalajara and Monterrey -- and nearly half are in cities of more than 100,000 people.
Mexicans are also predominantly young, with one in three under the age of 15.
The 16.5 million population of Mexico City, a capital dogged by soaring crime and serious pollution, is hardly growing.

The rising populations are concentrated either in border states like Baja California in the north and Quintana Roo in the south or in provinces like Morelos and Queretaro which take in people migrating from Mexico City in search of a cleaner, safer life.
